title: Athenian Democracy: An Experiment for the Ages
description:
S01 E01 — Why Athenian Democracy Matters
Considering the nature of Athenian democracy; how it functions in practice; surveying some of its key tenets; Professor Garland compares the Athenian governmental system to western democracy today; he shows the similarities and crucial differences.

title: Athenian Democracy: An Experiment for the Ages
description:
S01 E02 — The Origins of Greek Democracy
Among Greek city-states, Athens is not alone in having a form of democratic rule; Greek governments run on a sliding scale from oligarchy and democracy to kingship and tyranny; Homer's epics; examining several early examples of a democratic assembly.

title: Athenian Democracy: An Experiment for the Ages
description:
S01 E03 — Solon: The Father of Democracy?
One must first examine Athens as a polis or city-state, within the broader context of Ancient Greece; reviewing the territory of Attica; the lay of the land for Athenian government in the 6th and 7th centuries B.C.; Solon's reforms.

title: Athenian Democracy: An Experiment for the Ages
description:
S01 E04 — Cleisthenes the Innovator
Fifty years after Solon's reforms, a tyrant named Peisistratus seizes power; the overthrow of his tyranny; the ensuing skirmish among different aristocratic groups; the rise of Cleisthenes; he carries the democratic experiment forward.

title: Athenian Democracy: An Experiment for the Ages
description:
S01 E05 — The Nearly Bloodless Coup
According to Professor Garland, the end of the Greco-Persian Wars in the early 5th century B.C. is Athens' finest hour; the reforms of 462 B.C., when Ephialtes and Pericles attack Areopagus and bring radical democracy — an unprecedented experiment.

title: Athenian Democracy: An Experiment for the Ages
description:
S01 E06 — Democracy at War
The ancient Greeks consider military service a privilege; hoplite warfare and the construction of their navy go hand in hand with the rise of democracy in Athens; particularly since the Athenian military has no permanent commander-in-chief.

title: Living History: Experiencing Great Events of the Ancient and Medieval Worlds
description:
S01 E01 — Ramesses II: Heartbeat of History
A leap into the ancient world; discovering the moment-by-moment heartbeat of history; the Battle of Kadesh, the Egyptian pharaoh Ramesses II's disastrous campaign against the Hittites; the king spins a tactical retreat into a glorious victory.

title: Living History: Experiencing Great Events of the Ancient and Medieval Worlds
description:
S01 E02 — Marathon: The Persians Have Landed!
A look into the Battle of Marathon; the outnumbered Athenians scramble for help before heading to the coast for an impressive fight against the invading Persians; the Athenians' surprise running charge into battle and the strenuous marches.

title: Living History: Experiencing Great Events of the Ancient and Medieval Worlds
description:
S01 E03 — Oresteia: Judgment at the Dionysia
The Theater of Dionysus on a warm March day; one of the most astounding theatrical performances; Aeschylus's Oresteia is an innovative dramatic trilogy; the trial of Orestes is a relevant consideration of Athenian democracy at a time of great unease.

title: Living History: Experiencing Great Events of the Ancient and Medieval Worlds
description:
S01 E04 — Attack On Attica: Pericles's Gamble
The time of Pericles and the Peloponnesian War; political action requires rural citizens to head into the city; the cramped urban conditions and pestilence breeds disaffection among the polity; inspiring Athenians for the continued glory of the city.

title: Living History: Experiencing Great Events of the Ancient and Medieval Worlds
description:
S01 E05 — Socrates On Trial: For the Defense
Exploring a new context for understanding Socrates, one of the Greeks' most famous citizens; during the Peloponnesian War, tension lingers following the overthrow of an oligarchy in Athens; the democratic population is in search of a scapegoat.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E01 — What is a Pirate?
Exploring the reasons piracy endures from ancient times until today; why it is so difficult to both define and eradicate; how one can understand the rule of law and the rights of nations and individuals on the high seas and in borderless realms.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E02 — Pirate Facts and Fictions
Examining popular pirate legends; discovering which aspects include some truth and which contain none at all; pirate literature can teach a lot about the Jolly Roger, gold-filled treasure chests, the pirate Edward Thatch and more.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E03 — Real Pirates of the Caribbean
How the Spanish's power hold on the Caribbean is broken; which nationalities join in the free-for-all; the historical importance of Alexander Exquemelin's "Buccaneers of America" and Captain Charles Johnson's "A General History of the Pyrates".

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E04 — Pirate Attacks and Tactics
Pirates want money or anything they can turn into money; consequently, they usually wish for a speedy surrender, do not want a battle and rarely sink captured ships; the many tactics pirates use to apprehend their prey in the age of sails.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E05 — Buried Treasure and Pirate Economics
Very few pirates hit it big or try to bury their treasure on a deserted island; exploring the business aspect of piracy, which is one of the few aspects of life pirates can control; piracy is a no-prey, no-pay system; the risk of no pay is very real.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E06 — Pirate Freedom Fighters
The complex truths of piracy and the pirate life are much different from the common tale surrounding them; the real goals of those pirates who attack and overthrow maritime powers; how the pirate motto, "a merry life and a short one," comes to be.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E07 — Pirates and Enslavement
Pirates often let their captives go as they know what can go wrong with too many unhappy captives on a ship; pondering whether this prisoner release also applies to non-European men; the deep and complex relationships between pirates and enslavers.

title: The Real History of Pirates
description:
S01 E08 — The Sea Dogs of Elizabeth I
Privateers and pirates at the time of Queen Elizabeth I thrive by finding trade and protection; the individual histories of the most famous, ambitious and wealthiest of the Sea Dogs; these are John Hawkins, Sir Francis Drake and Sir Walter Ralegh.

title: Pirates: Fact and Fiction
description:
S01 E01
From the Dread Pirate Roberts to Robert Louis Stevenson, Professor Nush Powell goes back through history and sorts out fact from fiction across pop-culture portrayals of pirates.

title: Pompeii: Daily Life in An Ancient Roman City
description:
S01 E01 — Reflections On and of Pompeii
When most people hear the name of the archeological site of Pompeii, they think of destruction; gaining an overview of the course; considering why the remains of Pompeii offer more than just a story of a cataclysm.

title: Pompeii: Daily Life in An Ancient Roman City
description:
S01 E02 — Geology and Geography On the Bay of Naples
Land and humankind help to shape Pompeii; examining the violent geological forces that forge the distinctive region of the Bay of Naples; tracing its influence on the surrounding geography; the various cultures that contribute to life in this area.

title: Pompeii: Daily Life in An Ancient Roman City
description:
S01 E03 — The Rediscovery of Vesuvian Lands
Archeological finds from the area are unearthed starting around 1594; uncovering the history of Pompeii's excavation in the 1700s, from the kings who plunder its artwork to the modern scholars who seek another kind of treasure.

title: Pompeii: Daily Life in An Ancient Roman City
description:
S01 E04 — Etruscan Pompeii - 5th Century B.C.
While the last days of Pompeii attract popular attention, the city is a thriving cultural center centuries before its destruction; delving deep into Pompeii's remote Etruscan history; exploring what life is like in this ancient pre-Roman settlement.

title: Pompeii: Daily Life in An Ancient Roman City
description:
S01 E05 — Samnite Pompeii - 2nd Century B.C.
Centuries after the establishment of Etruscan Pompeii, the city is invaded by the Samnites; witnessing the conquest of the city by these invaders; considering how Pompeii is redefined and expanded by its new inhabitants.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description: Eastern civilization has a fascinating story with important consequences; the accomplishments of Eastern civilization, from the material economy of day-to-day life to the political and religious philosophies that bind Eastern cultures together.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E02 — Yin and Yang - The Geography of China
Starting with the geography and climate of China, the cradle of Eastern civilization; looking at the geographical regions of China; exploring the country's two great river systems, which divide Chinese culture into two distinct regions.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E03 — Early China and the Mysterious Xia
The beginnings of Chinese history; what archeological evidence shows about humans in the Paleolithic and Neolithic eras; looking at the fragmented cultures of early civilizations, including the mysterious Xia dynasty.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E04 — The Coming of the Shang
Looking at evidence that the Shang dynasty is responsible for the development of Chinese writing, a complex social structure and the first large cities in East Asia; visiting the cities and tombs of the first significant Chinese dynasty.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E05 — The Shang and Writing for the Gods
Learning about the enigmatic "oracle bones"; the origins of Chinese writing; turning to the Shang society's social organization, religious practices and cosmology; how the concept of yin and yang emerges during the Shang dynasty.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E06 — The Zhou and the Mandate of Heaven
Unpacking the Mandate of Heaven, a belief that seizure of power could be justified as an expression of divine will; how it resonates in Chinese political history for 3,000 years; the Zhou's overthrow of the Shang dynasty; the Zhou dynasty's legacy.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E07 — Great Ideas of the Zhou - Confucianism
During the Warring States Era, Chinese thinkers consider the nature of society and government; Confucianism is the guiding philosophy of China and much of East Asia for more than 2,500 years; learning about Confucius's life, philosophy and followers.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E08 — Great Ideas of the Zhou - Later Confucianism
Two contrasting views of human nature and political theory; while Mencius believes humans are innately good, Xunzi believes human nature is evil; both philosophers remain faithful to Confucius's belief in the need for well-educated, ethical rulers.

title: Experiencing Rome: A Visual Exploration of Antiquity's Greatest Empire
description:
S01 E01 — Rome-A Spectacular Civilization
Examining the visual nature of Roman society and the key role of spectacular display; ranging from its center in the Roman Forum to its frontiers.

title: Experiencing Rome: A Visual Exploration of Antiquity's Greatest Empire
description:
S01 E02 — A Brief Survey of the Roman Empire
This lecture provides a chronological, thematic and geographical framework; understanding the visual components of the Roman Empire; especially how different forms of governments and their citizens affect their art, architecture and public display.

title: Experiencing Rome: A Visual Exploration of Antiquity's Greatest Empire
description:
S01 E03 — Power, Conquest, and Romanization
Learning the fundamental role of Rome's military in expanding the empire through conquest; creating and projecting the image of Roman power; introducing non-Romans to Roman values and identity.

title: Experiencing Rome: A Visual Exploration of Antiquity's Greatest Empire
description:
S01 E04 — Triumphal Processions-Victory Parades
Conquest provides a reason for triumphal processions, sacrifices, games and other grand spectacles; it also allows for public and religious participation in a reinforcement of Roman values and identity.

title: Experiencing Rome: A Visual Exploration of Antiquity's Greatest Empire
description:
S01 E05 — Imperial Palaces
Touring the palaces of Rome's powerful rulers; seeing how power and culture are displayed in forms that are admired and imitated by lower social classes.

title: Experiencing Rome: A Visual Exploration of Antiquity's Greatest Empire
description:
S01 E06 — The Roman House-Space and Decoration
As a stage for political, religious and social display, the houses of Roman elites celebrate Roman virtues and cultural identity; reinforcing to social equals and inferiors the influence of the inhabitants.

title: Experiencing Rome: A Visual Exploration of Antiquity's Greatest Empire
description:
S01 E07 — Roman Houses as Greek Palaces
Touring the largest house in Pompeii and an enormous pleasure villa along the Bay of Naples; seeing how Greek material becomes the standard for Roman prestige display in public and private venues.

title: Experiencing Rome: A Visual Exploration of Antiquity's Greatest Empire
description:
S01 E08 — Pompeian Houses and Greek Myth
The House of Octavius Quartio in Pompeii offers an example of what has been termed middle-class emulation of the elite use of Greek material.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description: Eastern civilization has a fascinating story with important consequences; the accomplishments of Eastern civilization, from the material economy of day-to-day life to the political and religious philosophies that bind Eastern cultures together.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E02 — Yin and Yang - The Geography of China
Starting with the geography and climate of China, the cradle of Eastern civilization; looking at the geographical regions of China; exploring the country's two great river systems, which divide Chinese culture into two distinct regions.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E03 — Early China and the Mysterious Xia
The beginnings of Chinese history; what archeological evidence shows about humans in the Paleolithic and Neolithic eras; looking at the fragmented cultures of early civilizations, including the mysterious Xia dynasty.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E04 — The Coming of the Shang
Looking at evidence that the Shang dynasty is responsible for the development of Chinese writing, a complex social structure and the first large cities in East Asia; visiting the cities and tombs of the first significant Chinese dynasty.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E05 — The Shang and Writing for the Gods
Learning about the enigmatic "oracle bones"; the origins of Chinese writing; turning to the Shang society's social organization, religious practices and cosmology; how the concept of yin and yang emerges during the Shang dynasty.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E06 — The Zhou and the Mandate of Heaven
Unpacking the Mandate of Heaven, a belief that seizure of power could be justified as an expression of divine will; how it resonates in Chinese political history for 3,000 years; the Zhou's overthrow of the Shang dynasty; the Zhou dynasty's legacy.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E07 — Great Ideas of the Zhou - Confucianism
During the Warring States Era, Chinese thinkers consider the nature of society and government; Confucianism is the guiding philosophy of China and much of East Asia for more than 2,500 years; learning about Confucius's life, philosophy and followers.

title: Foundations of Eastern Civilization
description:
S01 E08 — Great Ideas of the Zhou - Later Confucianism
Two contrasting views of human nature and political theory; while Mencius believes humans are innately good, Xunzi believes human nature is evil; both philosophers remain faithful to Confucius's belief in the need for well-educated, ethical rulers.

title: Experiencing Rome: A Visual Exploration of Antiquity's Greatest Empire
description:
S01 E01 — Rome-A Spectacular Civilization
Examining the visual nature of Roman society and the key role of spectacular display; ranging from its center in the Roman Forum to its frontiers.

title: Masterpieces of Ancient Greek Literature
description:
S01 E01 — Definitions, Boundaries, and Goals
Learning to define ancient, Greek and masterpiece before moving on to discuss the importance of reading these works; knowing the best ways to do so.

title: Masterpieces of Ancient Greek Literature
description:
S01 E02 — Homer I-Introduction to Epic and Iliad
Introducing the Homeric epics; examining how the theory that they are composed orally might influence one's reading; summarizing essential mythological background before moving on to an overview of the "Iliad" and a deeper discussion of Book 1.

title: Masterpieces of Ancient Greek Literature
description:
S01 E03 — Homer II-Iliad, The Wrath of Achilles
Exploring the themes and action of books 2-9 of the "Iliad"; the poet's imaginative presentation of chronology; a remarkable concentration of scenes that explore the possibility of peace or cooperation in the midst of war.

title: Masterpieces of Ancient Greek Literature
description:
S01 E04 — Homer III-Iliad, The Return of Achilles
Completing the "Iliad"; focusing on Achilles's return to battle and its aftermath; learning that Homer's Achilles is not only Greece's greatest warrior but also a man struggling with the values of his culture and the awareness of his own mortality.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E01 — Touring the Cradle of Western Civilization
The dynamic civilizations that emerge in the Aegean; the scope of the human drama that is played out there; some of the towering figures and remarkable sites to encounter; Professor Hale's recommendations for traveling this world as the ancients did.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E02 — Athens - Around the Acropolis and Parthenon
The Acropolis is a symbol of Athens; the path of the ancient annual procession honoring Athena; the history and meanings of the site's iconic buildings; the superlative architectural features of the Parthenon and its surprising original uses.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E03 — In the Footsteps of Socrates - Historic Athens
Treasures surrounding the Acropolis; the Theater of Dionysos, where one ponders the rituals of early dramatic festivals; the Odeon of Herodes Atticus, a venue of music and recitations; the Pnyx, an ancient hilltop assembly point; the agora market.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E04 — Around Attica - Temples and Mysteries
Visiting sacred monuments of Greece's beautiful Attica region; the Amphiareion is a shrine of a prophet deity; ancient oracle and healing practices; imposing shrines to Artemis and Poseidon; Eleusis is the site of mystical religious rituals.

title: 1066: The Year That Changed Everything
description:
S01 E01 — The Norman Conquest Through History
What makes 1066 a pivotal year in the history of Western civilization; how the meaning of the Norman Conquest is debated and interpreted over time; how two weddings lay the groundwork for this moment; information for grasping the Norman Conquest.

title: 1066: The Year That Changed Everything
description:
S01 E02 — England and Normandy Before the Conquest
A closer look at the chaotic half-century between 1016 and 1066; two figures are crucial during this time; Edward the Confessor, who succeeds to the English throne in 1042; William the Bastard, who brings the Norman nobles under control.

title: 1066: The Year That Changed Everything
description:
S01 E03 — The Succession Crisis in England
How the relationship between Edward the Confessor and William the Bastard puts England and Normandy on a collision course; Edward's plans for succession; meeting the contenders to the throne; Harold Godwinson at the Battle of Stamford Bridge.

title: 1066: The Year That Changed Everything
description:
S01 E04 — The Battle of Hastings
Revisiting one of the most important moments in English history; Dr. Paxton investigates some mysteries and controversies about the invasion; she explains the tactics of medieval warfare; she provides a blow-by-blow account of the battle.

title: Alexander the Great and the Macedonian Empire
description:
S01 E01 — Alexander the Great - Conqueror or Tyrant?
Pondering Alexander's identity and story; learning about the ancient sources that contribute to people's understanding of Alexander's life and legacy; examining the ways this figure is perceived by modern scholars.

title: Alexander the Great and the Macedonian Empire
description:
S01 E02 — Greece in the Age of Hegemonies
The story of Alexander starts centuries before his birth, in the Greek city-states throughout the Aegean; the conflicts and political crises that shape the Greek world in the generations before Alexander; his father Philip's conquest of the region.

title: Alexander the Great and the Macedonian Empire
description:
S01 E03 — Achaemenid Persia
The Persian Empire of the 4th century offers a fierce opponent to Alexander in his conquest; the history of this mighty empire in the two centuries before Alexander's rise; the political and administrative structures that contribute to its success.

title: Alexander the Great and the Macedonian Empire
description:
S01 E04 — The World of Early Macedon
Although they ultimately unite Greece, Philip and Alexander are not considered full-fledged Greeks, learning about their barbarian homeland of Macedon and investigating its relationship to the more culturally influential city-states of Greece.

title: Play Ball! The Rise of Baseball as America's Pastime
description:
S01 E01 — Ground Rules: Baseball Before Babe Ruth
Why the year 1920 is considered a pivotal year in baseball; achieving a sense of uniformity in the game; examining the years before 1920, when changes in the game were rapid, dramatic, and often surprising.

title: Play Ball! The Rise of Baseball as America's Pastime
description:
S01 E02 — Early Bat and Ball Games
A look back at the beginnings of baseball; how and why the early version of the game evolved in the middle of the 19th century C.E.; learning how early clubs like the Gothams and the Knickerbockers helped repurpose a child's game for urban adults.

title: Play Ball! The Rise of Baseball as America's Pastime
description:
S01 E03 — The Era of Amateur Baseball Clubs
Exploring the rise of amateur baseball clubs in the United States; the outings of Brooklyn's Eckford Club; the rise of the Knickerbocker Club of New York City and the significance of their 1845 decision to write down the rules of the game.

title: Play Ball! The Rise of Baseball as America's Pastime
description:
S01 E04 — The Dawn of Professional Baseball
How the game of baseball moved toward professionalism; what made professionalization polarizing; studying future Hall of Famer Harry Wright, who helped pave the way for professional baseball's success by assembling a talented group of players.

title: Play Ball! The Rise of Baseball as America's Pastime
description:
S01 E05 — Baseball's Many Leagues and Associations
How baseball found a formula for 20th-century success after three tumultuous decades; leagues and associations; the transformations of minor leagues into major ones; the competitive relationships between leagues; the national agreement of 1883.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E01 — Hitler and the Nazi Youth
The horrors of Nazi Germany are one hallmark of World War II; pondering how ordinary German citizens find themselves participating in such heinous events; going inside the propaganda machine of Hitler's Germany; seeing how it targets the youth.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E02 — Japanese Soldiers in Nanjing
The origins of World War II lie in Asia in 1931; tracing the invasion of 1937 and the Rape of Nanjing; witnessing the events through the eyes of a Chinese soldier and a Japanese journalist, young men who bear witness to the flesh and blood of battle.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E03 — Panzer Leaders Who Changed Warfare
In addition to the story of people, World War II is the story of technology; perhaps nowhere is this more apparent than the tanks Germany uses to barrel across Poland and France in "lightning warfare"; how new technology defeats the old ways of war.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E04 — Jews Inside the Warsaw Ghetto
Wartime Warsaw offers a gateway to the darkest events of the war; bearing witness as the city's Jews are rounded up and put in the ghetto, where the specter of disease and starvation always looms; stories from several of the ghetto's inhabitants.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E05 — The Small Acts of the French Resistance
In Nazi-occupied France, informants create an environment of paranoia and fear, yet some people offer resistance in ways big and small; revisiting the legacy of the French Resistance to experience life under the Nazi boot.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E06 — A Child and a Pilot in the London Blitz
Shifting one's attention across the English Channel, where Britain faces the Nazi war machine alone; tracing the war in London through the eyes of a Jewish child in the East End, a bureaucrat performing unglamorous duties and a young Oxford student.

title: A Pastime of Their Own: The Story of Negro League Baseball
description:
S01 E01 — Emancipation and the American Pastime
The recorded history of Black American baseball goes back to the 1850s.

title: A Pastime of Their Own: The Story of Negro League Baseball
description:
S01 E02 — Drawing the Color Line
The story of Black baseball mirrors the story of America.

title: A Pastime of Their Own: The Story of Negro League Baseball
description:
S01 E03 — Black Ball Goes Pro
Segregation takes hold in the professional leagues, explore the world Black baseball players had to navigate in the late 19th century.
